I will keep to the cropping pattern I know best in Quzhou: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. I am 69, so I will not make my year more complicated by splitting into many crops that need more labor, more market judgment, and more risk. Wheat and maize fit our local climate, I understand their timing, and I can manage them with familiar machinery and routine field work. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want stable emergence and yield, but I will still farm in a steady, conservative way rather than chasing the highest possible output. For wheat, I will prepare the land well, put most fertilizer in early, irrigate at the key stages, and control disease and weeds with a small number of sprays. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize, keep the stubble and use simple tillage or no-tillage to save effort, then focus on one strong fertilizer program, a couple of irrigations if needed, and basic pest control. My goal is not to take big risks; it is to get a dependable harvest from a system I can still manage well myself.
